article_title: English MAP Reading Fluency technical report
citation: NWEA. (2024). English MAP Reading Fluency Technical Report. https://www.nwea.org
title: ZPD-leveled foundational skills progressions mapped to aligned instructional materials
description: The Phonological Awareness and Phonics & Word Recognition domains each offer within-domain adaptivity along a progression of skills, so reported data point toward a zone of proximal development (ZPD) level within the domain. "Each step in the Phonological Awareness and Phonics & Word Recognition progressions is mapped to best practice instructional materials made available by the Florida Center for Reading Research." This links assessment results directly to instruction at the student's current skill level, from single letters and letter sounds up to word reading and phoneme manipulation.
requirements: Within-domain adaptive administration is needed to locate each student's ZPD level in the progression
target_learners: early readers not yet ready to read passages
examples: ZPD levels are reported for Phonological Awareness and Phonics & Word Recognition with performance expectations by level
key_sources: NWEA. (2024). English MAP Reading Fluency Technical Report. https://www.nwea.org/research/publication/english-map-reading-fluency-technical-report/

article_title: Accelerate Success for English Learners: Students Work beyond the Edge of Their Current Abilities with Formative Assessment
citation: Barbara Jones, Molly Faulkner-Bond, and Jennifer Blitz. (2024). Accelerate Success for English Learners: Students Work Beyond the Edge of Their Current Abilities With Formative Assessment. WestEd, Region 15 Comprehensive Center. https://www.wested.org/
title: Zone of proximal development (ZPD) as the frame for edge learning with English learners
description: The brief organizes its argument around Vygotsky's ZPD, which it defines as "the realm of what a student can do in interaction with others." Learning is less effective when too easy or too frustrating; the ZPD is the level of challenge "just beyond what students already know and can do." The brief extends this to English learners, arguing teachers should not wait for full English proficiency before offering rigorous edge learning, and links the ZPD to formative assessment as edge work for both teacher and learner.
requirements: Ongoing formative assessment to keep track of the ever-changing edge of students' abilities
constraints: The edge is always changing, so understanding of where it is requires ongoing intentional effort
target_learners: English learners (multilingual learners) in K-12 classrooms
target_learning_goals: Engagement with rigorous, grade-level disciplinary content and language development simultaneously
examples: The brief's early elementary poetry lesson structures teacher and peer support so students analyze grade-level poetic devices at the edge of their competencies
key_sources: Barbara Jones, Molly Faulkner-Bond, and Jennifer Blitz. (2024). Accelerate Success for English Learners: Students Work Beyond the Edge of Their Current Abilities With Formative Assessment. WestEd, Region 15 Comprehensive Center. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED673601

article_title: PsyScore: A Psychometrically-Aware Framework for Trait-Adaptive Essay Scoring and ZPD-Scaffolded Feedback
citation: Wei Xia, Jin Wu, Haoran Shi, Xiangyu Wang, Chanjin Zheng. (2026). PsyScore: A Psychometrically-Aware Framework for Trait-Adaptive Essay Scoring and ZPD-Scaffolded Feedback. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20287
title: ZPD-aligned strategy mapping: deterministic mapping of latent ability θ to explicit instruction, targeted scaffolding, or intellectual challenge
description: PsyScore defines a deterministic mapping from estimated ability to a pedagogical control token: explicit directive instruction for struggling learners (θ < −1.0), targeted scaffolding for developing learners (−1.0 ≤ θ ≤ 1.0), and intellectual challenge via Socratic questioning for advanced learners (θ > 1.0). The article states the "ZPD boundary values are designed to operationalize scaffolding theory within a computational framework", and traits with discrimination above 1.2 receive higher prompt attention.
requirements: A validated latent ability estimate (θ) from the IRT scorer is required to select the strategy
constraints: Strategy thresholds (−1.0, 1.0) are design values grounded in the authors' operationalization of scaffolding theory, not empirically derived optima
target_learners: Essay writers across proficiency levels, from struggling to advanced
target_learning_goals: Proficiency-appropriate writing feedback: error correction, guided improvement, or rhetorical refinement
examples: Table 10 maps θ < −1.0 to explicit directive instruction on grammar and mechanics, −1.0 ≤ θ ≤ 1.0 to targeted scaffolding balancing praise with 1-2 improvement areas, and θ > 1.0 to intellectual challenge via open-ended questions
key_sources: Wei Xia, Jin Wu, Haoran Shi, Xiangyu Wang, Chanjin Zheng. (2026). PsyScore: A Psychometrically-Aware Framework for Trait-Adaptive Essay Scoring and ZPD-Scaffolded Feedback. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20287

article_title: A Reconsideration of Cognitive Load Theory
citation: Schnotz, W., Kürschner, C. (2007). A Reconsideration of Cognitive Load Theory. Educational Psychology Review 19, 469–508. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-007-9053-4
title: Zone of proximal development perspective on cognitive load theory
description: The article reconsiders cognitive load theory "from the perspective of Vygotski's concept of the zone of proximal development". On this reading, learning happens within a zone in which tasks are neither too easy nor too difficult, so the relation between load and learning is not simply monotonic: load that is within the learner's zone supports learning, while minimal load may fall outside it.
requirements: Instructional tasks must be matched to the learner's zone of proximal development rather than simply minimizing load
target_learners: learners working at the edge of their current capabilities
target_learning_goals: skill and knowledge acquisition within the zone of proximal development
key_sources: Schnotz, W., Kürschner, C. (2007). A Reconsideration of Cognitive Load Theory. Educational Psychology Review 19, 469–508. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-007-9053-4

article_title: The Social Construction of Data: Methodological Problems of Investigating Learning in the Zone of Proximal Development
citation: Peter Smagorinsky. (1995). The Social Construction of Data: Methodological Problems of Investigating Learning in the Zone of Proximal Development. Review of Educational Research, 65(3), 191-212. http://rer.aera.net
title: Vygotsky's zone of proximal development as a genetic-method account of a socially mediated, elastic and unbounded mind
description: The article elaborates Vygotsky's ZPD as "each person's range of potential for learning, where that learning is culturally shaped by the social environment in which it takes place." Development proceeds through a genetic (developmental) method in which mental processes are mediated by tools and signs, so knowledge passes from the intermental to the intramental plane via assisted performance. The mind is elastic (its direction depends on the sociocultural environment) and unbounded (theoretically limitless in potential, and spatially distributed through tools: Wertsch's point that the mind "extends beyond the skin"). The article uses this framework to critique research methodology.
requirements: The learner must be consonant with the cultural tools mediating development: tools work when they are sanctioned by the cultural environment, recognized by the learner as tools, and used volitionally.
constraints: The article notes the ZPD has been interpreted in three completely different ways and invoked for theoretically incompatible pedagogies, so any neo-Vygotskian claim is one social construction among competing readings.
target_learners: learners in culturally shaped social environments
target_learning_goals: development of culturally mediated higher mental processes
appropriation of cultural knowledge through assisted performance
examples: The article cites Vygotsky's illustration of a child performing at a more advanced level with adult or peer assistance than alone, and internalizing the knowledge transacted through that assisted performance.
key_sources: Peter Smagorinsky. (1995). The Social Construction of Data: Methodological Problems of Investigating Learning in the Zone of Proximal Development. Review of Educational Research, 65(3), 191-212. https://doi.org/10.3102/00346543065003191

article_title: The Social Construction of Data: Methodological Problems of Investigating Learning in the Zone of Proximal Development
citation: Peter Smagorinsky. (1995). The Social Construction of Data: Methodological Problems of Investigating Learning in the Zone of Proximal Development. Review of Educational Research, 65(3), 191-212. http://rer.aera.net
title: Smagorinsky's neo-Vygotskian account of the ZPD as an elastic and unbounded mind
description: The article develops an account of Vygotsky's zone of proximal development in which the mind is 'both elastic in that cognitive growth may take different directions depending on the sociocultural environment in which it occurs, and unbounded in terms of its extent and potential for growth'. Elasticity means higher mental processes have no fixed operations but embody culture-specific ways of thinking; unboundedness means the zone's upper reaches continually evolve and the mind extends beyond the skull through mediational tools. The article uses this account to ground its critique of research methodology.
requirements: Development requires the learner's consonance with, and volitional use of, the cultural tools that mediate it
constraints: The account assumes development is socially mediated; unadulterated development could only take place in vacuo, a state not possible in human society
target_learners: learners in culturally diverse educational settings
target_learning_goals: development of culturally shaped higher mental processes
examples: The article contrasts this view with Piagetian conceptions in which direct instruction can inhibit a child's own exploration
key_sources: Peter Smagorinsky. (1995). The Social Construction of Data: Methodological Problems of Investigating Learning in the Zone of Proximal Development. Review of Educational Research, 65(3), 191-212. https://doi.org/10.2307/1170682

article_title: Uniting epistemological perspectives to support contextualized knowledge development
citation: Sara van der Linden, Susan McKenney. (2020). Uniting epistemological perspectives to support contextualized knowledge development. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09772-7
title: Zones of Proximal Performance and Implementation as reflection outcomes
description: The article defines two constructs building on Vygotsky's zone of proximal development and McKenney's zone of proximal implementation. The Zone of Proximal Performance targets "the difference between the pre-determined, explicated teaching behaviors individual teachers can execute on their own, and those they could identify and perform with guidance". The Zone of Proximal Implementation targets the analogous difference for learner, classroom, and school-related insights. Deliberate reflection informs the ZPP; aware reflection informs the ZPI; comparing both guides action.
requirements: Reflection activities that surface both performance relative to standards and situated contextual insights
constraints: The zones are conceptual constructs derived from prior theory, not measured in this article
target_learning_goals: Understanding gaps between current and potential teaching performance and implementation
examples: Conclusion drawing in the reflection procedure is framed as determining considerations within the ZPP (deliberate) or ZPI (aware)
key_sources: Sara van der Linden, Susan McKenney. (2020). Uniting epistemological perspectives to support contextualized knowledge development. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-020-09772-7

article_title: The Effect of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) on Reading Comprehension in English for Specific Purposes Courses
citation: Fahimeh Farahani. (2018). The Effect of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) on Reading Comprehension in English for Specific Purposes Courses. International Journal of Education & Literacy Studies, 6(1). http://dx.doi.org/10.7575/aiac.ijels.v.6n.1p.79
title: Zone of Proximal Development as a rationale for cooperative NLP reading tasks
description: The article draws on Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development (as cited in Chaiklin, 2003) as a second theoretical basis, holding that "learners should enter other peers' proximal zone in order to learn effectively". Because one aspect of NLP is cooperation, the article assumes learners can enter each other's proximal zone through NLP and benefit from more resources of knowledge. This links the cooperative organization of the reading tasks to peer expertise as an aid to learning.
requirements: Cooperative task organization so learners can access peers' proximal zones
constraints: Presented as an assumption linking NLP cooperation to ZPD, not separately tested in this study
target_learners: undergraduate EFL learners in ESP courses
examples: Reading tasks in the experimental group were conducted cooperatively to maximize similarities between learners and minimize differences
key_sources: Fahimeh Farahani. (2018). The Effect of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) on Reading Comprehension in English for Specific Purposes Courses. International Journal of Education & Literacy Studies, 6(1). http://dx.doi.org/10.7575/aiac.ijels.v.6n.1p.79

article_title: Investigating the Effect of Cooperative Learning and Competitive Learning Strategies on the English Vocabulary Development of Iranian Intermediate EFL Learners
citation: Neda Fekri. (2016). Investigating the Effect of Cooperative Learning and Competitive Learning Strategies on the English Vocabulary Development of Iranian Intermediate EFL Learners. English Language Teaching, 9(11). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v9n11p6
title: Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development and sociocultural theory as the rationale for cooperative language learning
description: The article grounds cooperative learning in Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development, defined as "the distance between the actual developing levels as defined by independent problem solving and the level of potential development as defined through problem solving under adult assistance, or in cooperation with more skilled peers". Interaction itself is treated as establishing learning, which is "typically social rather than individual in nature". The article uses this framework to motivate expecting group interaction among peers to simplify language acquisition in the EFL classroom.
requirements: Learners must interact in the target language within groups, including cooperation with more skilled peers, for the ZPD mechanism to operate as described
constraints: The article presents the ZPD as theoretical background rather than testing it directly in the experiment
target_learners: Iranian intermediate EFL learners in language institutes
target_learning_goals: English vocabulary development through socially supported interaction
examples: The study operationalised the rationale by teaching vocabulary to an experimental group through cooperative group work over eight weeks and comparing posttest performance with competitive and traditional conditions
key_sources: Neda Fekri. (2016). Investigating the Effect of Cooperative Learning and Competitive Learning Strategies on the English Vocabulary Development of Iranian Intermediate EFL Learners. English Language Teaching, 9(11). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v9n11p6

article_title: The Effect of Dynamic versus Static Assessment on Syntactic Development of Iranian College Preparatory EFL Learners
citation: Mohamad Reza Jafary, Noreen Nordin & Reza Mohajeri. (2012). The Effect of Dynamic versus Static Assessment on Syntactic Development of Iranian College Preparatory EFL Learners. English Language Teaching, 5(7). http://dx.doi.org/10.5539/elt.v5n7p149
title: Dynamic assessment grounded in Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development as an alternative to static testing
description: The article frames dynamic assessment (DA) as a Vygotskian, Feuerstein-derived approach that assesses learning potential rather than current performance. It states that "dynamic assessment includes a range of methods and materials to assess this potential for learning, rather than a static level of achievement assessed by conventional tests." DA mediates within the assessment itself and evaluates the enhanced performance that results, in contrast to static psychometric testing of already-developed abilities.
requirements: Mediation by a teacher or more competent peer within the assessment interaction
constraints: The article notes a remaining void in the field of speech and language therapy for DA of cognitive ability
target_learning_goals: Syntactic/grammatical development in English as a foreign language
examples: The study operationalised DA as twelve mediated multiple-choice grammar tests with strategy-based mediation and take-home information papers
key_sources: Mohamad Reza Jafary, Noreen Nordin & Reza Mohajeri. (2012). The Effect of Dynamic versus Static Assessment on Syntactic Development of Iranian College Preparatory EFL Learners. English Language Teaching, 5(7). http://dx.doi.org/10.5539/elt.v5n7p149

article_title: Effect of Glogster and Cooperative Learning Differentiated Instruction on Teachers' Perceptions
citation: Ghada M. Awada and Kawthar H. Faour. (2016). Effect of Glogster and Cooperative Learning Differentiated Instruction on Teachers' Perceptions. Teaching English with Technology, 18(2), 93-114. http://www.tewtjournal.org
title: Vygotsky's zone of proximal development and Tomlinson's differentiated instruction as the study's theoretical framework
description: The study grounds its intervention in Vygotsky's zone of proximal development and Tomlinson's theory of differentiated instruction. Under ZPD, scaffolds are provided "beyond independent learning yet within their zone of proximal development", with the task remaining the same while the level of assistance changes. Tomlinson's framework holds that "the teachers must address four def inite elements: students, learning environment, content, and instruction", and that ignoring any element diminishes learning quality. The Glogster and cooperative learning model operationalises these frameworks through tiered assignments, flexible grouping, and scaffolding.
requirements: Teachers must provide mediation or scaffolds matched to individual personal needs within learners' zones of proximal development
constraints: The article states that should any of the four elements be ignored, the quality of learning will be diminished
target_learners: Grade 8 EFL learners of low socioeconomic status in Lebanese public schools
target_learning_goals: English and Science project research and oral presentation skills
examples: The experimental treatment used tiered assignments, flexible grouping, and scaffolding strategies over eight weeks at six contact hours per week
key_sources: Ghada M. Awada and Kawthar H. Faour. (2016). Effect of Glogster and Cooperative Learning Differentiated Instruction on Teachers' Perceptions. Teaching English with Technology, 18(2), 93-114. http://www.tewtjournal.org

article_title: Symmetrical or Asymmetrical Scaffolding: Piagetian vs. Vygotskyan Views to Reading Comprehension
citation: Pishghadam, R., & Ghadiri, S. (2011). Symmetrical or asymmetrical scaffolding: Piagetian vs. Vygotskyan views to reading comprehension. Journal of Language and Literacy Education [Online], 7(1). https://jolle.coe.uga.edu
title: Zone of Proximal Development and symmetrical vs. asymmetrical peer interaction
description: The article frames scaffolding within Vygotsky's sociocultural theory, contrasting Piaget's symmetrical peer relationships with Vygotsky's asymmetrical ones. It defines the ZPD as "the discrepancy between what a child can do independently and what he/she can do under adult guidance or in collaboration with more capable peers". Scaffolding is the supportive behavior that helps learners progress into their ZPD, and the study operationalizes the two theories as homogeneous versus heterogeneous pairings during cooperative reading.
requirements: Pairs must remain constant and tasks must sit just above learners' current independent ability for scaffolding to support movement through the ZPD
constraints: The study tested the framework only for EFL reading comprehension with intermediate adult learners in an institute setting
examples: 52 learners were paired homogeneously (scores within one standard deviation) or heterogeneously (scores differing by more than one standard deviation) and read eight Interchange passages cooperatively
key_sources: Pishghadam, R., & Ghadiri, S. (2011). Symmetrical or asymmetrical scaffolding: Piagetian vs. Vygotskyan views to reading comprehension. Journal of Language and Literacy Education [Online], 7(1). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1097243

article_title: Scaffolding competence-based learning design in the dental simulation curriculum.
citation: Foxton Richard, San Diego Jonathan P., Lu Emily, Rajadurai Susha, Bartlett Anitha, McIlwane Clare, Austin Rupert, Srisontisuk Pinsuda, Sagoo Anika K., Piper Kim. (2025). Scaffolding competence‐based learning design in the dental simulation curriculum. European Journal of Dental Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/eje.12985
title: Scaffolding competence across simulation affordances via the zone of proximal development
description: The article applies Vygotsky's zone of proximal development to simulation curriculum design: competence is scaffolded by sequencing learning activities from haptic virtual reality simulators through phantom-head plastic and natural teeth, matching each activity to what the simulation technology's affordance can support. The ZPD is defined as the gap between what a student can independently achieve and what can be attained with support from a teacher or capable other, addressed by scaffolding. In this design the simulation technology itself can act as the capable other, allowing some activities to become self-directed.
requirements: Learning outcomes must be mapped to align with activities and assessments across the simulator sequence
constraints: Access and availability of simulation technologies may differ across dental schools, so the cross-over may not be applicable
target_learning_goals: clinical competence in restorative dentistry procedures such as interproximal caries preparation
examples: Manual dexterity drilling on haptic tiles is unsupervised with the simulator as the 'abled-other', while caries removal tasks are supervised by clinical teachers using minimal intervention principles
key_sources: Foxton Richard, San Diego Jonathan P., Lu Emily, Rajadurai Susha, Bartlett Anitha, McIlwane Clare, Austin Rupert, Srisontisuk Pinsuda, Sagoo Anika K., Piper Kim. (2025). Scaffolding competence‐based learning design in the dental simulation curriculum. European Journal of Dental Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/eje.12985

article_title: Progression and individual differences in children's series completion after dynamic testing.
citation: Touw, K. W. J., Vogelaar, B., Thissen, F., Rovers, S., & Resing, W. C. M. (2020). Progression and individual differences in children's series completion after dynamic testing. The British Journal of Educational Psychology, 90(1), 184-205. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjep.12272
title: Dynamic testing grounded in Vygotsky's zone of proximal development, with IRT modelling of change
description: The article presents dynamic testing as an assessment approach drawing "upon Vygotsky's theory of the zone of proximal development (ZPD)". Dynamic tests "examine the changes that occur during an assessment by incorporating feedback and training into the testing phases, providing information about the individual's ZPD". Because classical gain scores are criticized for ceiling effects and regression to the mean, the study uses item response theory models that "enable estimating the probability of solving an item correctly, based on the child's ability and the item difficulties", giving a more favourable reliability of gain scores in dynamic testing contexts.
requirements: A pre-test-training-post-test design with parallel item structures; IRT modelling (here Embretson's MRMLC) with condition as a covariate
constraints: Gain-score interpretation depends on item difficulty range; the authors note four-point gains from 1 to 5 items can mean something different than gains from 13 to 18 points on a 20-item test
target_learning_goals: measuring learning processes, modifiability, and potential for change
examples: The study operationalized change as MRMLC-estimated gain scores from pre-test to post-test
key_sources: Touw, K. W. J., Vogelaar, B., Thissen, F., Rovers, S., & Resing, W. C. M. (2020). Progression and individual differences in children's series completion after dynamic testing. The British Journal of Educational Psychology, 90(1), 184-205. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjep.12272
